messages:
marie (CS): Hey team — onboarding ACME Analytics. Running our Python quickstart and hitting a couple things: first, after rotating the key they still get 403 on some endpoints. Second, occasional 429 bursts during load tests.

samir (SE): Can you paste the exact error and the minimal code you used? quick checks: are you using the org-scoped key vs project token?

marie (CS): here's the snippet they run in prod test harness:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.generate("Summarize the last 24h logs")
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```
Error: 403 {"error":"permission_denied","detail":"token missing scope: inference.run"}  — but the rotated key shows same scopes in the admin UI.

dev-rel-jess: 403 with "token missing scope" usually means the key is from the org-level vault without project access. Did you rotate a global owner key or a project-specific one? Also check header: we accept `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key` depending on SDK version. Which SDK version?

marie (CS): They're on `redwood-sdk==0.9.2` and setting `REDWOOD_API_KEY` env var. Admin UI shows scope list: ["billing", "read_organization", "inference.run"].

eng-oncall-ryan: Might be a caching/replication lag after rotation — tokens can take a few seconds to propagate. But 429 bursts are separate: looks like the harness fires 40 parallel workers at once. SDK has a default concurrency limit; if they bypass it (starting many processes) they can hit per-key rate limits. What's the 429 body?

marie (CS): 429 body: `\{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":0.85\}`. They see ~10% of requests fail with 429 under ramp.

samir (SE): Two actionable things: 1) confirm token propagation by trying a fresh key in a single process, wait ~30s after rotation. 2) throttle client side: set `max_workers=4` or use the SDK's builtin rate limiter. Example in Python:
```py
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., max_concurrency=4)
# or wrap calls with backoff and sleep between batches
```

dev-rel-jess: Also confirm they aren't accidentally mixing endpoints (e.g., calling streaming chat endpoint with a text-gen token). Mismatch can return 403/400 depending on scope. If they copied keys between envs, make sure no stale env var or secret manager entry.

marie (CS): I asked them to run a single-process test after rotation and to set `max_concurrency=2`. They reran and 403s dropped to zero after 20s; 429s reduced to ~1%. They still see a few with `retry_after` ~0.4s.

eng-oncall-ryan: That's expected under short bursts. Recommend exponential backoff with jitter and a per-key token bucket. For immediate relief: enable client-side batching (small batches) or increase reserved capacity if persistent. Also we can whitelist their org for higher burst during onboarding — CCing product ops.

marie (CS): they asked if we can temporarily raise the burst. Can we do a one-off for a 24h window?

dev-rel-jess: Yes, ops can add a temporary rate override tied to the org id. Send me the org_id and target window. I added a KB link: <https://redwood.internal/kb/rate-limits#onboarding-bursts> :link:

cs-bot: Suggested next steps checklist:
• confirm token type (project vs org)
• wait 30s after rotation and retest
• set SDK `max_concurrency` to 2-4 during onboarding
• implement retry with exponential backoff (+ jitter)
• request temp burst override from dev-rel if needed

marie (CS): Thanks — I'll follow up with ACME, collect org_id and ask them to toggle concurrency. Will loop back after they test. :thumbsup:
